text:
safe-anything 

 Find the holes before someone else does. 
One command finds XSS, SQL injection and other vulnerabilities in your code, leaked secrets, 
risky mobile and cloud config, vulnerable dependencies, and the AI agent setup that writes it all. 
Every finding comes with the line, the reason and the fix. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Install · Releases · Claude Code plugin · GitHub Action · All 74 rules · Agent setups 
Made in Türkiye 🇹🇷 by erKam Yaman , who also made rust-anything · ❤️ Sponsor me · Sponsored by CodeRabbit 

 
 
 
 A real run on OWASP Juice Shop and on an agent setup with the usual mistakes (Apple M4). What it finds on other repositories . 
 

 
 
 
 Your code 
 SQL and command injection, XSS, eval , SSRF, path traversal, unsafe deserialization, weak crypto. Nine languages and SQL.
 
 
 Your secrets 
 Cloud and AI keys, tokens, private keys, passwords, and .env mistakes: committed env files, real values in .env.example , secrets behind NEXT PUBLIC or VITE . Always redacted in the output.
 
 
 Your stack 
 Android and iOS settings, Docker, GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, Terraform, nginx, and every locked dependency against OSV.dev.
 
 
 Your agent 
 MCP servers, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and OpenCode settings, hooks and skills: the files that decide what your agent may do.
 
 
 

 Quick start

 

That's it. No config, no account, no upload. It exits with 1 when something high or critical is
found, so it works as a pre-commit or CI check as is.

 

- .gitignore is respected, and node modules , vendor , target , dist , build , virtualenvs
 and .claude/worktrees are skipped. List more paths in .safe-anything-ignore .
- safe-anything:ignore in a comment silences that line (or the next one).
- In tests, specs and fixtures only real provider keys and private keys count, unless you pass
 --include-tests .

 What it finds

74 rules, each with a CWE id, an OWASP category and a link to the OWASP page that explains it.
The full list is in docs/rules.md.

 
 --- --- 
 Code SQL injection, command injection, XSS ( innerHTML , dangerouslySetInnerHTML , v-html , echo $ GET , raw ), eval and new Function , path traversal, SSRF, unsafe deserialization (pickle, yaml.load , ObjectInputStream , BinaryFormatter , unserialize , Marshal ), TLS checks turned off, MD5/SHA-1, DES/RC4/ECB, JWT none , template injection, debug mode, insecure cookies, Math.random tokens. JS/TS, Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, Ruby, C , SQL 
 Secrets AWS, GitHub, Slack, Stripe, OpenAI, Anthropic and Google keys, private keys, passwords in code, credentials in connection strings, committed .env files, real values in .env.example , a .gitignore that misses .env , secrets behind public prefixes ( NEXT PUBLIC , VITE , EXPO PUBLIC ) that ship in the client bundle 
 Agent setups bypassPermissions and --dangerously-skip-permissions , pre-approved Bash , MCP servers run with unpinned npx / uvx / docker , MCP tokens in plain text, remote MCP over curl \ sh in hooks and skills, prompt-injection text, skills that read /.ssh or cloud credentials, invisible Unicode in instructions. More 
 Mobile Android debuggable , cleartext traffic, exported content providers, WebView file access and JS bridges, world-readable files; iOS ATS turned off; tokens in UserDefaults, SharedPreferences, AsyncStorage or localStorage 
 Config Docker (unpinned base, root, secrets in ENV , ADD ), GitHub Actions ( pull request target , write-all , actions on @main , script injection from PR titles), privileged containers, hostNetwork , open Terraform ingress, public buckets, nginx autoindex, TLS 1.0/1.1 
 Dependencies every locked version in package-lock.json , yarn.lock , pnpm-lock.yaml , Cargo.lock , requirements .txt , poetry.lock , uv.lock , go.mod , Gemfile.lock , composer.lock and pubspec.lock , checked against OSV.dev, with the nearest fixed version 

 
 
 
 Of the 73 Next.js examples that come with env files, scanned one by one, the env checks flag one: a password behind NEXT PUBLIC . 
 

 For AI agents

safe-anything is also an MCP server, so your agent can scan before it commits, and before you
install someone else's skill or MCP server.

 

Or, as a Claude Code plugin with the skill that tells the agent how to triage and fix findings:

 

Tools: scan (path, offline, severity, include tests) and list rules . The skill is in
skills/safe-anything.

 In CI

 

Findings then show up in the repository's Security tab and on pull requests.

 Measured

Release build on an Apple M4, --offline , 2026-11-22. Every finding was read by hand. Times are
the scan's own report; the same scan took 0.03 to 0.13 s depending on what else the machine was
doing.

 Repository Files Findings What they are 
 --- --- --- --- 
 OWASP Juice Shop (vulnerable on purpose) 1,195 67 the login and search SQL injections, the eval challenges, MD5 passwords, tokens in localStorage, seeded passwords, open Terraform ingress; 2 to 3 false positives (a checksum MD5, innerHTML with trusted hint text) 
 DVWA (vulnerable on purpose) 233 63 the SQL injections, command injections, MD5 passwords and eval ; about 4 false positives (setup-script inserts, input validated in the "impossible" level) 
 expressjs/express 216 0 
 pallets/flask 231 2 both false positives in practice: eval of the user's own shell startup file, SHA-1 for key derivation (reported as low) 
 modelcontextprotocol/servers 439 1 pull request target in a workflow, worth a look 
 anthropics/skills 392 6 innerHTML in local review pages (5), shell=True in a script that runs commands by design 
 vercel-labs/agent-skills 439 0 
 rust-anything 3,134 6 innerHTML in GIF demo pages (5), an action on @master 
 safe-anything itself 53 0 checked in CI on every push 

 
 
 
 Quiet on good code: expressjs/express, 216 files, no findings. 
 

The noisiest rule is code.xss-inner-html : it fires on any HTML built from a variable, and most of
those in local tooling are not reachable by an attacker. It stays on, because real XSS looks the

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
cargo install safe-anything    # or: npx safe-anything .
safe-anything .

That's it. No config, no account, no upload. It exits with 1 when something high or critical is found, so it works as a pre-commit or CI check as is.

safe-anything . --json             # machine-readable report
safe-anything . --sarif            # GitHub code scanning
safe-anything . --offline          # no network (skips the dependency check)
safe-anything . --severity medium  # hide low findings
safe-anything . --fail-on never    # always exit 0 (or low, medium, high, critical)
safe-anything . --include-tests    # also report findings in tests and fixtures
safe-anything --list-rules
  • .gitignore is respected, and node_modules, vendor, target, dist, build, virtualenvs and .claude/worktrees are skipped. List more paths in .safe-anything-ignore.
  • safe-anything:ignore in a comment silences that line (or the next one).
  • In tests, specs and fixtures only real provider keys and private keys count, unless you pass --include-tests.
